extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies and Office of the Federal Register staff (officials preparing and filing documents for publication); librarians and legal practitioners who use or cite the Federal Register and CFR
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural rules governing what documents are filed with and published in the Federal Register and how the Code of Federal Regulations is compiled, updated, indexed, and made available. Covers definitions, filing/publication requirements, formats, indexing, citation, schedules, and agency responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (what is a 'document', 'filing', 'document having general applicability and legal effect')
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this chapter — 'Document' includes any Presidential proclamation or Executive order, and any rule, regulation, order, certificate, code of fair competition, license, notice, or similar instrument issued, prescribed, or promulgated by an agency. 'Filing' means making a document available for public inspection at the Office of the Federal Register during official business hours; a document is filed only after it has been received, processed and assigned a publication date according to the schedule in part 17. 'Document having general applicability and legal effect' means any document issued under proper authority prescribing a penalty or course of conduct, conferring a right, privilege, authority, or immunity, or imposing an obligation, and relevant or applicable to the general public, members of a class, or persons in a locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the baseline for determining which materials must be filed/published and how to treat filings (including the procedural step of receiving/processing/assigning publication dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's general authority (return of unacceptable documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register is delegated authority to administer this chapter and related provisions; the Director may return to the issuing agency any document submitted for publication if in the Director’s judgment the document does not meet the minimum requirements of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure submissions meet Chapter I minimum requirements because the Director can refuse filing/publication for failure to meet format/content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication policy — required contents of the FEDERAL REGISTER
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall publish a serial publication called the FEDERAL REGISTER to contain: (1) Executive orders, proclamations, and other Presidential documents; (2) Documents required to be published therein by law; (3) Documents accepted for publication under § 5.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the core scope of what the Federal Register must contain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness standard for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document required or authorized to be filed for publication shall be published in the FEDERAL REGISTER as promptly as possible, within limitations imposed by considerations of accuracy, usability, and reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing promptness with accuracy, usability, and cost; agencies should prepare materials to enable prompt publication consistent with those constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required to be filed and published
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents required to be filed for public inspection and published include: (a) Presidential proclamations and Executive orders in the numbered series and other Presidential documents submitted for publication; (b) Each document or class of documents required to be published by act of Congress; (c) Each document having general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories identify the mandatory filings — agencies must file any material falling into these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of other documents at Director's discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Director considers that publication of a document not covered by § 5.2 would be in the public interest, the Director may allow that document to be filed for public inspection and published in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-mandatory items may be published if the Director finds public interest — agencies may request but publication is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication not authorized (exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 15 of title 44 does not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements or proclamations thereof by the President; prohibits publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER of comments or news items; the Director may not accept any document for filing unless it is the official action of the agency concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not submit excluded materials (treaties, comments, news) for FR publication and should ensure submissions are official agency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEDERAL REGISTER as supplement to the Code of Federal Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FEDERAL REGISTER serves as a daily supplement to the Code of Federal Regulations. Each document that is subject to codification and published in a daily issue shall be keyed to the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents intended to become codified in the CFR must be prepared and keyed appropriately when published in the FR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily publication schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER published for each official Federal working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes continuous publication cadence; agencies should plan submissions to fit daily issues and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and mailing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government Printing Office shall distribute the FEDERAL REGISTER by delivery or deposit at a post office at or before 9 a.m. on the publication day, except that a FR dated for a Monday shall be deposited at or before 9 a.m. on the preceding Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets distribution timing expectations for users and subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of citation
rubrics_metrics.description: FEDERAL REGISTER material may be cited by volume and page number, and the short form 'FR' may be used for 'FEDERAL REGISTER' (e.g., '37 FR 6803').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes how to reference FR material for legal citation and cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of documents in the FEDERAL REGISTER
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document published shall be placed under one of these categories: (a) The President — Executive orders and Presidential documents; (b) Rules and regulations — documents having general applicability and legal effect (including documents subject to codification, general policy statements, interpretations, statements of organization/function); (c) Proposed rules — notices of proposed rulemaking (section 553 or other law) that, if promulgated, would have general applicability and legal effect; (d) Notices — miscellaneous documents applicable to the public not covered by (a)–(c) (e.g., announcements of meetings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must classify submissions correctly so they appear in the appropriate FR section and are indexed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of publication of the FEDERAL REGISTER
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee publishes the FEDERAL REGISTER in paper, microfiche, and online on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material must be prepared knowing multiple publication media; the Director may regulate formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing requirements for daily issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Each daily issue of the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be appropriately indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures discoverability of daily content; Office of the Federal Register is responsible for indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical subject indexes and annual cumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical subject indexes covering the contents of the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be published as currently as practicable and shall be cumulated and separately published at least once each calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term subject indexing obligation to help users locate material across time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily lists of parts affected and monthly cumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each daily issue shall carry a numerical list of the parts of the Code of Federal Regulations specifically affected by documents published in that issue; beginning with the second issue of each month, each daily issue shall also carry a cumulated list of the parts affected during that month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides immediate and cumulative pointers to CFR parts changed by FR publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly list of sections of the CFR affected (LSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A monthly list of sections of the Code of Federal Regulations affected shall be separately published on a cumulative basis during each calendar year and shall identify the sections specifically affected by documents published in the FEDERAL REGISTER during the period covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA is the authoritative monthly tool for checking whether a CFR section has been amended since the last revision date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes, digests, and guides (ancillaries) — publication authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may order the preparation and publication of indexes, digests, and similar guides based on laws, Presidential documents, regulatory documents, and notice materials; they will be published yearly or at other intervals as necessary and are special editions when public need requires special printing or binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits supplementary finding aids and special editions to meet user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR policy — periodic special edition
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to chapter 15 of title 44, the Director shall publish periodically a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER to present a compact and practical code called the 'Code of Federal Regulations' to contain each Federal regulation of general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes CFR as the periodic codification vehicle for regulations with general applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR currency objective (dependability and costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee intends that every practical means be used to keep the Code as current and readily usable as possible, within limitations imposed by dependability and reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates a balance between currency/usability and cost/dependability in CFR publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly development of CFR (titles and rearrangement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assure orderly development of the CFR, the Director may establish new titles and rearrange existing titles and subordinate assignments, but must consult with each agency directly affected before taking such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency consultation is required before structural changes to the CFR that affect agencies' content placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR periodic updating schedule and cutoff dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book of the Code shall be updated at least once each calendar year; if no change occurred during the year a notation may serve; more frequent updating may occur when the Director determines content has been substantially superseded; titles updated as of a given date will reflect all amendatory documents published in the Federal Register on or before the 'As of' date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies annual minimum updating, potential for more frequent updates, and the cutoff principle for what amendments are included in an updated title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of CFR publication and Director's format authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee authorizes publication of the CFR in paper, microfiche, and online on GPO Access; the Director may regulate the format to meet user needs and GPO facilities and provide for printing in many separately bound books as necessary; Director may, when necessary, set requirements for microfiche images and oversee organization/online access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency submissions should be compatible with multiple output formats and may be subject to format rules set by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cooperation obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall cooperate in keeping publication of the Code current by complying promptly with deadlines set by the Director of the Federal Register and the Public Printer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely agency compliance with FR/CFR deadlines is mandatory to ensure currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the Federal Register information services limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Office staff will provide information concerning the publications and original acts/documents, except they may not summarize or interpret substantive text of any act or document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office can give procedural and locating assistance but will not provide legal interpretation — users should contact issuing agencies for legal explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection procedures and filing time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed pursuant to law are available for public inspection at the Office during office hours with no formal inspection procedures; the Director shall cause each document received to be filed for public inspection not later than the working day preceding the publication day for that document; the Director shall cause notation of day and hour when filed on original and certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines public availability timing (no later than the working day before publication) and recordkeeping (filed time/date stamping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and certification of acts and documents (NARA rules & fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations for public use of National Archives records (36 CFR parts 1252–1258) govern furnishing reproductions and certificates of authentication; section 1258.14 provides for advance payment of appropriate fees for reproduction services and certifying reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for certified copies or reproductions follow NARA fee/payment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrestricted republication of FR material
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may reproduce or republish, without restriction, any material appearing in any regular or special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material in the FR is free for republication, subject to any other applicable law; agencies should not assume proprietary restrictions on FR text.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to use the CFR – consult LSA and cumulative lists for currency
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether a Code volume has been amended since its revision date, consult the 'List of CFR Sections Affected (LSA)' issued monthly and the 'Cumulative List of Parts Affected' in the Reader Aids of the daily FR; these lists identify the FR page number of the latest amendment of any given rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users and agencies must use the CFR together with LSA/cumulative lists to determine the current rule text and effective changes since the volume's revision date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective and expiration dates caution and insertion of notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication dates and effective dates are usually not the same; care must be exercised in determining the actual effective date. Where the effective date is beyond the cutoff date for the Code, a note is inserted to reflect the future effective date; where a regulation published in the Federal Register states a date certain for expiration, an appropriate note will be inserted following the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and users must pay attention to the difference between publication and effective/expiration dates and look for inserted notes indicating future effective or expiration dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB control numbers placement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paperwork Reduction Act requires Federal agencies to display an OMB control number with their information collection request; many agencies publish numerous OMB control numbers as amendments to existing regulations in the CFR and these numbers are placed as close as possible to the applicable recordkeeping or reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information collection requirements in rules should include the OMB control number near the relevant regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obsolete provisions not carried; use lists to find past provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions that become obsolete before the revision date stated on the cover of each CFR volume are not carried; users may find text of provisions in effect on a past date by using appropriate numerical list(s) of sections affected (LSA volumes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historic regulatory text is recoverable via LSA resources; current CFR volumes omit provisions obsolete before the volume's revision date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and administrative routing for the Administrative Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee of the Federal Register consists of the Archivist (Chairman), an officer of the Department of Justice designated by the Attorney General, and the Public Printer; the Director of the Federal Register is the Secretary of the Committee; material required by law to be filed with the Committee and correspondence intended for the Committee shall be sent to the Director of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural routing for Committee materials is centralized through the Director; agencies should send Committee-related filings and inquiries to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States Government Manual content standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual shall contain appropriate information about the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches; for major Executive agencies it shall include: (1) descriptions of the agency's public purposes, programs and functions; (2) established places and methods whereby the public may obtain information and make submittals or requests; (3) lists of officials heading major operating units. Brief supplemental information and selected Press Office materials may also be included at the Director's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide the specified descriptive and contact information for inclusion in the Manual and may expect public-facing summaries and selected press materials to appear.
